exact_prompt:
I'm shopping for cottage cheese in the United States.

Which brand should I buy, and why?
reviewed_answer:
When shopping for cottage cheese in the United States, a few standout brands consistently dominate taste tests, nutritional metrics, and consumer praise.

The best brand to buy depends slightly on what you value most—whether that is top-tier texture and protein, clean ingredients, or budget.

1. The Overall Winner: Good Culture

Why buy it: Good Culture is widely considered the gold standard of modern cottage cheese. It has a thick, incredibly creamy texture (thanks to a rich live and active culture blend) rather than being watery or soupy.   

The Pros: It packs an impressive amount of protein (typically 14 grams per half-cup), uses clean and simple ingredients without gums or thickeners, and has a mild, pleasantly tangy flavor. It is also pasture-raised and low in sodium compared to many legacy brands.   

Best for: Eating straight out of the tub, high-protein bowls, or anyone who dislikes the watery texture of traditional brands.   

2. The Clean & Classic Choice: Daisy

Why buy it: If you want a traditional, quintessential cottage cheese without any artificial additives, gums, or stabilizers, Daisy is the undisputed king.   

The Pros: The ingredient list is refreshingly minimal: skim milk, cream, salt, and active cultures (no guar gum or locust bean gum). It features a bright, clean, classic tartness with firm, tender curds suspended in a rich, soft cream.   

Best for: Purists who want clean ingredients and a reliable, nostalgic flavor.

3. The Best Budget Option: Trader Joe’s or Aldi (Friendly Farms)

Why buy it: If you want great cottage cheese without paying premium prices, private-label options from Trader Joe's or Aldi punch well above their weight class.

The Pros: Trader Joe’s Small Curd Cottage Cheese is exceptionally neutral, making it remarkably versatile for sweet (fruit-topped) or savory (black pepper and hot sauce) pairings. Aldi's Friendly Farms line offers a remarkably creamy texture and traditional tang at a fraction of the cost of name brands.   

Best for: Everyday grocery shoppers looking for maximum value.

4. The Best Mass-Market / Value Pick: Walmart (Great Value)

Why buy it: Frequently topping blind taste tests for mainstream availability, Walmart's store brand is surprisingly stellar.   

The Pros: It strikes a great balance of being not overly salty, highly versatile, and exceptionally budget-friendly. (Note that it tends to be a bit more liquidy than Good Culture, but it performs wonderfully when mixed into recipes or paired with fruit).   

Best for: Shoppers who want a dependable, cheap staple available at almost any corner of the country.

Summary Recommendation

Go with Good Culture if you want the absolute best taste, texture, and protein profile.

Go with Daisy if you want a clean ingredient label free of gums and stabilizers.

Go with Trader Joe's, Aldi, or Walmart if you want a great everyday staple on a budget.   

What do you plan to use your cottage cheese for—eating it plain, pairing it with fruit, or baking/blending it into recipes?
